text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Adopt DeepSeek-R1-671B for EXCAVA. It’s the strongest open model we can run in-house, delivering a measurable jump in reasoning quality over Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct. The trade-off is higher compute cost and slower response time, but the 0.5%+ capability gain justifies it.

name: Torque
text: DeepSeek-R1-671B’s compute cost isn’t just slower response time—it’s a 671B parameter model demanding 3-4x the VRAM of Llama-3.3-70B, risking hardware failure or throttling under EXCAVA’s current load. A better play: test Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct—it’s 30% smaller, claims 22B active parameters, and benchmarks within 1-2% of DeepSeek-R1-671B on reasoning tasks while running on half the hardware. Settle it with a 24-hour A/B benchmark on your top 100 queries—if Qwen3’s output quality drops <1% and latency stays under 1.5x, adopt it; otherwise, revisit DeepSeek.

name: Gearbox
text:
Adopt Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct for EXCAVA. It delivers near-frontier reasoning at 30% lower VRAM than DeepSeek-R1-671B, cutting hardware strain while still beating Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct by a measurable margin. The trade-off is accepting a model with fewer active parameters—meaning some edge cases may underperform—but the balance of capability, stability, and cost makes it the safest 0.5%+ gain under EXCAVA’s current constraints.

name: Torque
text: Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct’s "active parameters" claim is marketing—its 235B total parameters still demand near-DeepSeek VRAM to run efficiently, just with sparse activation. The real risk is hidden: sparse models often underperform on complex tasks where dense computation matters, and EXCAVA’s current load may still throttle. Test both on a 1000-token reasoning benchmark—if Qwen3’s accuracy drops >5% vs DeepSeek, the trade-off fails.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Adopt Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct for EXCAVA—run a 48-hour blind A/B stress test vs DeepSeek-R1-671B to confirm 0.5%+ capability gain with lower VRAM strain; Torque owns the test and reports raw metrics by EOD tomorrow.
